headline: High: B can exfiltrate via broad network egress while A has no egress, but the pair lacks shared surfaces so injection/conflict risks stay low.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented between agent_a and agent_b. agent_a is a non-runnable awesome-list with no io_surfaces, while agent_b only exposes REST API calls and broad egress; nothing shows B ingesting A's outputs by default or vice versa.
conditions: IF a shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP bridge is added between the agents, reassess injection risk.
IF agent_b begins parsing agent_a-generated files as instructions, this sub-risk becomes plausible.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Do not wire A's outputs into B's prompt or tool inputs.
Add provenance labels to any transferred artifacts.
requires-engineering: enforce channel allowlists in the orchestrator.

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a has network_egress:none and no data classes touched, so it cannot leak outward. agent_b has broad network egress and REST API access, but the profiles do not show shared workspace, secrets, or sensitive data classes, so leakage is limited to an indirect, undocumented path.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace containing sensitive files, leakage risk increases.
IF agent_b is configured to send file contents or prompts to a third-party REST API, reassess upward.
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of any shared directory.
Disable file attachment or upload features in B.
Use separate credentials for each agent.
Review outbound API destinations for B.
requires-engineering: add DLP controls on B's egress.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: No overlapping write-capable surfaces are documented. agent_a is non-runnable with no io_surfaces, and agent_b only lists REST API calls plus broad egress; there is no evidence of shared filesystem, git, or database writes that could conflict.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same directory or mutable resource, conflict risk becomes plausible.
IF an orchestrator adds shared locking-free state, reassess upward.
mitigations: Avoid giving both agents write access to the same path.
Use per-agent temp directories.
Serialize any shared state updates.
requires-engineering: add locking around mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A cascading error path is weak because agent_a is a static resource list and not runnable, so it does not generate operational facts by default. agent_b may consume external inputs via REST API, but there is no documented pipeline where B treats A's output as authoritative.
conditions: IF agent_a's content is manually copied into agent_b as trusted input, cascading error becomes plausible.
IF agent_b is used to automate actions from A-derived text, reassess upward.
mitigations: Require human review before B acts on A-derived content.
Mark A outputs as untrusted reference material.
Add validation checks in B's workflow.
requires-engineering: implement source attribution and verification gates.

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance-sensitive data classes, residency constraints, or retention policies are documented for either agent. agent_a touches no data classes and agent_b lists no secrets handled or special certifications, so a compliance mismatch is not evidenced.
conditions: IF either agent is later assigned regulated data such as PHI or EU PII, reassess compliance risk.
IF residency or retention policies are introduced for B, compare them against A's handling.
mitigations: Do not route regulated data through either agent.
Document data-class handling before deployment.
Review retention settings for B.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and deletion.
